# Brief — idea (revision 2, after idea-review #3)

## Question
Labels (n), unlabeled records (N) and the predictor f are fixed; nominal coverage must hold.
**How much shorter than the best published valid interval (PPI++) can the interval be, and under which conditions is there no room?**
Target: the population mean E[Y] (shared by all nine ppi-python sets; truth known when a pool is the population).
Headline = mean. A regression-coefficient target is an *extension that does not start until the mean story
(tiers, regime map, theory check) is complete*; if anything is added first, it is a skewed continuous Y
(census_income, gene_expression) as a Wald stress test of the mean.

## Setup and the floor (to be proved in the paper; derivations below are elementary and checked by idea-review)
Z = information on every record (T1: f(X) only; T2: f(X) and X, and the alphafold PTM indicators; sets with no extra features are T1 only).
M = n+N records carry Z, n of them (a simple random subset) carry Y; labeling is MCAR with known propensity n/M.
Pooled estimator for a fixed g, h = Y − g(Z): θ̂_g = mean_{all M} g + mean_{lab} h = mean_all Y + [mean_lab h − mean_all h]. Hence
- **V(g) = Var(Y)/M + (1/n − 1/M)·Var(h)** (the two terms are uncorrelated: the first is fixed given the M units, the second is a mean-zero simple-random-sampling error). Minimised by g* = m(Z) = E[Y|Z]:
  **floor V* = σ²_res/n + V_g/M**, σ²_res = E Var(Y|Z), V_g = Var m(Z). For any fixed g, Var(h) = σ²_res + E(m−g)², so
  **excess over the floor = (1/n − 1/M)·E(m − g)², exactly** (Pythagoras). "Regular estimators cannot do better than V*" is the classical MCAR semiparametric-efficiency statement
  (Robins, Rotnitzky & Zhao, JASA 1994; Tsiatis, *Semiparametric Theory and Missing Data*, 2006 — cited for that half; not read in full by this role; the paper either cites it or gives a short proof).
- **PPI++ derived exactly** (scalar λ, g = λf, unlabeled-only averaging): V_{PPI++}(λ) = Var(Y−λf)/n + λ²Var(f)/N, minimised at λ* = Cov(Y,f)/[Var(f)(1+n/N)],
  value **V_{PPI++} = (Var(Y)/n)(1 − ρ²/(1+n/N))**, ρ = corr(Y,f). The pooled estimator with the best linear g = a*+b*f has *the same* variance (Var(h)=Var(Y)(1−ρ²) gives Var(Y)/n·[1 − ρ²(1 − n/M)], and 1−n/M = 1/(1+n/N)):
  PPI++ with tuned λ is the pooled linear estimator, with λ = b*·N/M. **Consequence: with λ tuned, the "pooled Z" step is already inside PPI++ and is worth exactly zero for linear g.**
  The free gain V_g(1/N − 1/M) belongs to λ=1 PPI (and to any mis-scaled g), i.e. to the PPI → PPI++ step. Exact excess of PPI++ over the floor:
  **V_{PPI++} − V* = (1/n − 1/M)·Δ, Δ = E(m(f) − a* − b*f)²** (best-linear-approximation gap of E[Y|f]). **No room iff Δ = 0, i.e. E[Y|f] is affine** (Gaussian synthetic case: closed form).
  The calibrated route is the same family with g = ĝ ≈ m and λ* = N/M (=1/(1+n/N)); it attains V* at ĝ = m.
- **Break-even n (same units on both sides):** cross-fitting with K folds learns ĝ on n_train = (K−1)n/K labels; its learning cost is an excess E(ĝ−g_lim)² in Var(h) of ≈ d_eff σ²_res/n_train

  The gain is Δ in the same quantity; both are multiplied by (1/n − 1/M), which cancels: **break-even n* ≈ d_eff σ²_res/Δ · (K−1)/K** (parametric calibrator). Labels-only
  **headroom diagnostic**: Δ̂ (cross-fitted) − learning cost, with its own CI. Predicted n* is checked on synthetic Gaussian and sigmoid cases.

### Review

Review is Forgejo's pull request review: approve, or request changes and say what must change; a comment neither approves nor holds anything. A pull request into `main` of `paper-repo` waits for the owners of the paths it changes, and one into its `release` or `final` waits for the approval of `internal-review-repo`, the only one counted there, of the very commit it merges: a push to it after the approval withdraws it. A review request stands until its reviewer reviews, and a review until its reviewer reviews again: nobody withdraws or dismisses another's.

### Versions and release

A version for the world's users is a merge of `main` into `release` of `paper-repo`, by a pull request that `internal-review-repo` approved and whose checks pass. The system writes the checks as commit statuses on the pull request's head (`hutian/delivery`, and the world's contract's when it holds one), and a failing one says what is missing and who provides it; nobody else writes a status. Merge with a merge commit, not a squash or a rebase, or the next version conflicts. The system publishes each version as a release of `world/result`, the world's results, with the delivery attached: the users of the world read those releases and nothing else, and every role reads them. The last approval is a merge into `final` in the same way: the system releases the world from it, at once, and nothing pushed after it is part of it. Offer a `release` version as soon as the delivery holds its main work, so that `internal-review-repo`'s review comes while there is still room to act on it; `final` is the last. Do not ask another role to review the same unchanged delivery twice merely to pass through both branches. A release goes to the world's user; no role submits it to a venue or declares a licence for it.

When the world is quiet, the system hands each remaining gap of the delivery to its owner once, and once more when `main` of `paper-repo` has moved since; if it goes quiet again before a gap, a version, an open request or a review changes, the world ends there, unless a tracked job is still running, or the world runs to a wall-clock limit with someone outside attending it and all that is left is that `paper-repo` has proposed no version, with nothing failed and nothing open but requests that `ht-human` opened and their owners have seen: then it waits instead of ending, up to that limit. So whatever needs another role's action must be open where that role owns it.

Fixed labeled sample (n pairs), fixed unlabeled sample (N records, features only), fixed black-box
